contract.known_boundary: Schedule bounded background work and manage long-lived worker/service lifecycle through platform-specific adapters.
contract.non_equivalence_policy: Mobile background schedulers, desktop service managers, and Raspberry Pi system services are not treated as semantically interchangeable.

candidates.raspberry_pi_evidence: Pinned upstream supports Linux/systemd; official Raspberry Pi documentation demonstrates systemd/systemctl services on Raspberry Pi OS. This is research target evidence only.

research_findings.mobile: Workmanager and native_workmanager provide independent Android/iOS scheduling families. auto_start_flutter adds a broader background/startup bridge. iOS execution remains OS-controlled and best-effort; no persistent-daemon equivalence is asserted.
research_findings.desktop: auto_start_flutter and dart_service_manager provide two independent families across Windows/Linux/macOS. kardianos/service adds a third native-service family.
research_findings.raspberry_pi: Depth is 2/2 through two independent systemd-capable service-manager families: dart_service_manager and kardianos/service. The target bridge is explicit because official Raspberry Pi OS documentation demonstrates systemd services/systemctl; hardware/runtime validation is still open.
research_findings.security: auto_start_flutter is fully CLEAR with OSV checked and no hits. Workmanager and dart_service_manager remain REVIEW due unresolved Pub versions; native_workmanager remains source REVIEW due committed build/devtools binary artifacts; kardianos/service is source/supply-chain CLEAR but OSV reports GO-2026-5024. RunWisp and service-manager-rs are BLOCKED and excluded from coverage.

decision.next_action: Keep discovery depth closed but admission open: resolve exact Pub versions, remediate or upgrade the kardianos dependency carrying GO-2026-5024, define platform-specific cancellation/retry/boot/power semantics, and run Android/iOS/Windows/Linux/macOS/Raspberry Pi lifecycle tests before any Library intake.
